To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose an approach to partially reconstruct a high-resolution 4-dimensional light field from a stack of photographs taken with a single fixed camera.

(i) a focus map can be calculated by combining gradient detection with graph cut; (ii) a depth map can be obtained from a focus map by exploiting a calibrated camera; (iii) the epipolar planes of the light field can be reconstructed from a stack of photographs taken by a single camera by using masked back-projection; (iv) the angular resolution of the reconstructed light field can be significantly increased by using a wide interval of focus distances

1) a single fixed camera can be used to capture a 4D light field; 2) the focus map can be computed from a stack of images taken by a fixed camera; and 3) the tomographic reconstruction can be performed from the focus map.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and validation of a new technique for reconstructing 4D light field data from a stack of images captured with a fixed camera.
the reconstruction of a high angular resolution 4D light field from a stack of 2D images.
the reconstruction of 4D light-fields from fixed-camera stacks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have developed an efficient and effective algorithm to reconstruct the high-resolution 4-D light field of a scene from a fixed-camera focus stack.
the proposed approach is an efficient way for the tomographic reconstruction from focal stacks.
the proposed approach is able to reconstruct high resolution light fields from a fixed camera focal stack.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to achieve a high angular resolution from a single camera, and a high spatial resolution from multiple cameras.
we are able to partially reconstruct a high-resolution 4-D light field from a single fixed-camera focal stack.
we can reconstruct a 4D light field from a stack of 3D photographs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a single camera is sufficient to capture high-quality 4D light field information from a scene, and that the quality of the light field can be improved with respect to the original photographs by using a simple tomographic reconstruction method.
the depth map is not needed for the reconstruction of the epipoles and the angular resolution of the reconstruction is not affected by the accuracy of the depth map.
the reconstruction quality of the tomographic approach is significantly better than the one achieved with the conventional reconstruction method based on the weighted average of all the images.
